_comment: br-frankenpandas-6k29f follow-through. ONE fixture, named explicitly.
payload with BOTH missing markers: [int64 3, null, int64 1, int64 2, na_n].
Its banked expectation preserves both spellings in the sorted tail
(... null, na_n), which is what the oracle produced when op_series_sort_values
hand-rolled pd.Series(values, index=index) and pandas inferred numpy float64 —
in a float64 lane a None and a NaN stay distinguishable on the way back out.
op_series_sort_values now routes through fixture_series_from_payload (landed by
a peer citing br-frankenpandas-6k29f), so the payload's declared dtype applies:
{int64} + a null selects the NULLABLE Int64, where BOTH missing values are
pd.NA and both render as 'null'. The fixture's 'na_n' tail is therefore an
artifact of the builder that was removed, not a property pandas still has.
This is a NULL_MARKER move only — the sorted VALUES and their order are
unchanged, and na_last placement is unchanged. FrankenPandas is unaffected
either way because fp_types::semantic_eq treats any two missing values as
equal (br-frankenpandas-xwxci, 93f77abeb), so this cannot be a way to force a
red fixture green: the fixture is green now and stays green.
Recorded because a stale expectation that no live oracle produces is exactly
the residue the freshness differ exists to surface.
